"no strata fees" is the tell, not a perk line. Card after card carries it because the typical product is non-strata: no strata corporation means no Form B, no depreciation report, no CRF and no strata insurance summary — the buyer personally replaces every one of those checks (title, permits, inspection) or does without them.
The 40% rule replaced the number many sellers still quote.

Card text names South Meridian Elementary and Earl Marriott Secondary for one address; the schools themselves are Ministry-confirmed by name and address, but no SD36 locator run for any card address on this page is on record.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in South Surrey Duplexes with Suites for Sale

items.t: Secondary suites — Surrey (the core rule for this topic): a secondary suite is a dwelling unit that is an accessory use, with habitable floor area not exceeding 40% of the principal dwelling unit, within a single family, semi-detached or duplex residential building, and not a separate strata lot. Only one secondary suite is permitted per single family, semi-detached or duplex dwelling unit; a secondary suite is not permitted within a coach house or garden suite; one suite may be permitted in dwellings within small-scale, multi-unit housing zones, including Comprehensive Development zones; and each application is reviewed for legal restrictions such as Land Use Contracts and Building Schemes. To become legal, the owner must meet the conditions of zoning, hold the necessary building permits, meet the BC Building Code, and pay the secondary suite utility and service fees.

Open-house disclosure — BCFSA Rule 5-10(3): Rule 5-10(3) of the Real Estate Rules, as set out in the Office of the Superintendent of Real Estate's November 2017 consultation report, states that disclosure of representation is not required when a licensee is only hosting an advertised open house or providing factual responses to general questions, unless the licensee solicits or receives information from the party about the party's motivation, financial qualifications or needs in respect of real estate.

ALR block: subdivision within the ALR requires Agricultural Land Commission approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s.6; SPA s.239; ALCA s.21(1)). ALC residence caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha). Farm class is three-tiered ($2,500 on 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 + 5% of value over 4 ha; $10,000 under 0.8 ha; by Oct 31) — a flat "$2,500+" line is an error.

Strata block (where a half duplex is a strata lot, and for bare-land strata parcels): Form B within 7 days, max $35 + 25¢/page; depreciation reports on a 5-year cycle for stratas with 5+ lots since July 1, 2024; minimum 10% CRF contribution since November 1, 2023; rental-restriction bylaws void since November 24, 2022; only 55+ age bylaws valid (SPA ss.123.1/123.2 + May 1, 2023 exemptions). A "45+" listing line is not a valid BC age bylaw.

(2) 2209 165 Street: top block "OPEN HOUSE: Nov 01, 2026, 01:00 PM - 03:00 PM PST"; listing text "Open House on Sunday, November 1, 2026 12:00PM - 2:00PM." (3) 101 16631 18 Avenue: top block "OPEN HOUSE: Nov 01, 2026, 02:00 PM - 04:00 PM PST"; listing text "Open House on Sunday, November 1, 2026 1:00PM - 3:00PM." Cards with no open-house block at all: for those, only the absence can be stated.

A suite can never be split off as its own title. Surrey's definition makes a secondary suite part of the principal unit — not a separate strata lot — so the rental income is inseparable from the half-duplex interest itself; a buyer counting on selling or separately mortgaging the suite is counting on something the bylaw does not allow.
"no strata fees" cuts both ways.

faq.q: The listing says "legal suite" — can I rely on that?

faq.a: Its habitable floor area cannot exceed 40% of the principal dwelling unit, it must sit within the duplex building, and it cannot be a separate strata lot. A suite over the 40% line falls outside Surrey's definition whatever the listing text says.
faq.q: How big can the suite legally be?

faq.a: No — only one secondary suite is permitted per single family, semi-detached or duplex dwelling unit, and a suite is not permitted inside a coach house or garden suite. A card advertising both a legal suite and a second guest suite needs the second unit's status explained in writing before subjects come off.
faq.q: Can a half duplex have two suites?

faq.a: No. The City states the legislation does not provide retroactive legalization for suites built without the necessary building permits; owners must still go through the permit process.
